messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT  Dedicated pool 'us-west-dedicated-2' reporting 95%+ GPU utilization for 14m. Top tenant: NovaFin (tenant-nf-42). Queues growing at gateway. Paging on-call and eng-sre.

priya_oncall: I'm on pager. Initial ask: are requests failing or just queuing? Any customer reports? @sam_cs can you confirm?

sam_cs: NovaFin ops pinged us 5m ago. They see timeouts for non-interactive flows and degraded performance for dashboards. They confirm a large scheduled evaluation job started ~01:45 UTC; said it wasn't expected to run this long. They're asking for temporary relief.

dan_eng_sre: checking pool state. Running quick inspect: 

```
$ redctl pool show us-west-dedicated-2 --format json | jq '.'
{
  "pool": "us-west-dedicated-2",
  "total_gpus": 20,
  "allocated_gpus": 20,
  "tenants": [
    {"id":"tenant-nf-42","gpus":16,"queued":410,"avg_lat_ms":1450},
    {"id":"tenant-alpha","gpus":4,"queued":5,"avg_lat_ms":120}
  ]
}
```

Autoscaler disabled for this pool (locked-reserved). No spare nodes available to auto-attach.

eva_platform: listing immediate mitigation options: 1) short burst allotment (+4 GPUs) if burst quota exists; 2) enforce tenant-level kill switch for long offline jobs (we can pause via tenant-control API); 3) partial traffic redirection of non-sensitive calls to hosted with token-tagging; 4) ask NovaFin to terminate/patch their batch.

dan_eng_sre: quota check: tenant-nf-42 has 2 burst credits (each 30m, +4 GPUs). Attempting burst request.

```
$ redctl burst-request --pool us-west-dedicated-2 --tenant tenant-nf-42 --gpus 4 --duration 00:30:00
Request accepted: id=br-77a9 queued
```

allocator-bot: BURST_SCHEDULED br-77a9  allocation may be deferred up to 2m due to scheduler gating.

priya_oncall: while we wait, can we limit concurrency for heavy endpoints? We should avoid hard-failing customer interactive flows. Dan, can you push a per-tenant policy to slow batch endpoints?

dan_eng_sre: pushing a soft throttle via tenant policy labeling and rate-limit rules now. This will deprioritize requests with header X-Job-Type: batch.

```
$ redctl tenant update tenant-nf-42 --policy add rate_limit:batch=4/s --policy mode:soft-priority
Policy updated
```

sam_cs: I told NovaFin we applied a throttle for batch jobs and requested they cancel any accidental runs. They're coordinating internally; ops said they paused some workers.

eva_platform: burst allocated: +4 GPUs attached to pool. Observed initial drop in queued requests from 410 -> 240 over ~70s. Avg latency trending 1450ms -> 780ms.

priya_oncall: good. Set escalation: if queued > 200 after 10m of burst, escalate to eng-platform. Also log chargeback impact.

dan_eng_sre: creating a short-lived circuit-breaker that returns 429 for low-priority batch when queue > 300 to protect interactive UX. Deploying now.

```
$ redctl tenant update tenant-nf-42 --circuit-breaker batch --threshold 300 --response 429
Circuit breaker set
```

sam_cs: NovaFin reports dashboards are usable again for critical flows. They asked: will burst be charged? Need estimate to share.

eva_platform: yes bursts are billable. Dan, can you get approx tokens/GPU-hr used during the event? We'll provide a ballpark.

dan_eng_sre: pulling metrics and will attach to incident ticket. Quick estimate: additional 4 GPUs for 30m ~ 2 GPU-hours billed (per billing model) -> we will confirm exact USD later.

priya_oncall: note for handoff: burst active, soft throttle + circuit-breaker in place. NovaFin is cooperating and paused some jobs. Monitoring. Handing off to Dan for the next 40m.

dan_eng_sre: acknowledged, taking over. Adding a short monitor script in case queues rebound:

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
POOL=us-west-dedicated-2
T=tenant-nf-42
while true; do
  q=$(redctl pool show $POOL --json | jq ".tenants[] | select(.id==\"$T\") | .queued")
  if [ "$q" -gt 300 ]; then
    echo "CRITICAL: queued=$q" | mail -s "pool alert" eng-platform@redwood.internal
  fi
  sleep 20
done
```

sam_cs: scheduling follow-up with NovaFin for post-incident review. They want recommendations to avoid future on-call bursts (e.g., scheduled windows, dev gating, or using hosted fallback).

eva_platform: long term proposals: - default soft-gating for batch endpoints on dedicated pools; - optional scheduled batch windows for enterprise tenants; - allow limited cross-tenant soft-rebalance for emergencies. I'll open RFC.

dan_eng_sre: burst window ends in ~22m. Current snapshot: queued=62, avg_lat=360ms, GPUs in use=20. If stable after end we'll mark mitigated.

allocator-bot: BURST_END br-77a9  4 GPUs detached, pool returned to baseline.

priya_oncall: final check. post-burst snapshot?

dan_eng_sre: final: queued=14, avg_lat=310ms, no 5xx. Closing incident as mitigated. Creating INC-2002 with actions: 1) clarify burst billing in enterprise contracts, 2) add tenant onboarding checklist for batch windows, 3) implement auto-soft-rebalance RFC.

eva_platform: filing RFC link: https://git.internal/redwood/rfcs/tenant-dedicated-burst-policy. Please review.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED  Status: mitigated, customer impact: degraded dashboards and background job slowdowns for ~28 minutes, no user-facing errors recorded. Severity: sev-2.

:white_check_mark:
